modules.label: Zarya Module

fail.title: Zarya control fails
steps: You must restore Zarya's guidance computer.

modules.explain: Zarya was the first ISS module (1998), providing early power, storage and propulsion before other modules arrived.

modules.label: Zvezda Service Module

fail.title: Zvezda life support offline
steps: Trace air scrubbers back to Zvezda.

modules.explain: Zvezda provides life support, crew quarters and propulsion — the 'command module' inherited from Mir technology.

modules.label: Unity Node

fail.title: Unity docking clamp jammed
steps: An arriving cargo ship cannot dock.

modules.explain: Unity (Node 1) connects the US and Russian segments and provides docking ports for modules and visiting vehicles.

modules.label: Destiny Laboratory

fail.title: Experiment rack overheating
steps: A protein crystal experiment is at risk.

modules.explain: Destiny is the primary US research lab, hosting racks for biology, physics, and materials science experiments.

modules.label: Harmony Node
modules.explain: Harmony (Node 2) links Destiny, Columbus and Kibo, and serves as a docking point for cargo vehicles.

modules.label: Columbus Laboratory
modules.explain: Columbus, built by ESA, hosts European physics, biology, and fluid science experiments.

modules.label: Kibo Module

fail.title: Kibo airlock pressure mismatch
steps: A small satellite deployment is delayed.

modules.explain: Kibo, Japan's module, includes a lab, logistics section, robotic arm and airlock for small satellite deployment.

modules.label: Tranquility Node
modules.explain: Tranquility (Node 3) houses life-support hardware including the water recovery and oxygen generation systems.

modules.label: Cupola Observation Deck

fail.title: Cupola shutter stuck
steps: Micrometeoroid shield won't close before a debris pass.

modules.explain: The Cupola is a windowed dome used for Earth observation and to visually guide robotic arm operations.

modules.label: Quest Airlock

fail.title: Suit oxygen check failing
steps: A spacewalk is scheduled in 20 minutes.

modules.explain: Quest is the primary airlock for US spacesuits, used to depressurize before spacewalks (EVAs).

modules.label: Leonardo Logistics Module
modules.explain: Leonardo is a Permanent Multipurpose Module used for storage of spare parts and supplies.

modules.label: Rassvet Module
modules.explain: Rassvet is a Russian mini-research module used for docking and cargo storage.

modules.label: Poisk Module
modules.explain: Poisk provides an additional Russian docking port and airlock for spacewalks.

modules.label: Nauka Module
modules.explain: Nauka is Russia's multipurpose laboratory module, added in 2021 for research and storage.

modules.label: Pressurized Mating Adapter 1
modules.explain: PMA-1 connects Zarya to Unity, joining the earliest US and Russian segments.

modules.label: Pressurized Mating Adapter 2
modules.explain: PMA-2 provides a docking location at the forward end of Harmony for crew vehicles.

modules.label: Pressurized Mating Adapter 3
modules.explain: PMA-3 was relocated over the station's life to support new docking adapter installations.

modules.label: Integrated Truss Structure

fail.title: Truss segment vibration detected
steps: Inspect the truss segment with cameras.

modules.explain: The truss is the station's backbone, holding solar arrays, radiators and external equipment.

modules.label: Solar Array Wings (A & B)

fail.title: Solar Array A/B power drops to zero
steps: Lights dim across the US segment.
Trace the energy flow: array → charge controller → battery → distribution unit.

modules.explain: Solar arrays convert sunlight to electricity, feeding charge controllers that store energy in batteries for use during orbital night.

modules.label: Solar Array Wings (C & D)
modules.explain: Rotary joints continuously reorient the arrays toward the sun as the station orbits Earth every 90 minutes.

modules.label: Radiator Panels

fail.title: Radiator ammonia leak suspected
steps: Crew must isolate the affected loop.

modules.explain: Radiators release excess heat from electronics and crew activity into space, since there's no air to cool things naturally.

modules.label: Thermal Control System

fail.title: Internal loop temperature spike
steps: Cabin air feels warmer than normal.
Check the internal thermal control loop pump.

modules.explain: The Thermal Control System circulates coolant (ammonia externally, water internally) to keep all systems within safe temperature ranges.

modules.label: Battery Units

fail.title: Battery degradation detected
steps: Charge cycles are shorter than expected.
One battery unit reports reduced capacity.

modules.explain: Nickel-hydrogen batteries store solar energy so systems keep running during the 45 minutes per orbit spent in Earth's shadow.

modules.label: Power Distribution Units

fail.title: Power distribution imbalance
steps: One module is drawing excess power.

modules.explain: PDUs route electricity from batteries to every module, balancing supply with demand across the station.

modules.label: Nitrogen Storage Tanks
modules.explain: Nitrogen tanks supply gas used to pressurize the cabin atmosphere alongside oxygen.

modules.label: Hydrogen Storage Tanks
modules.explain: Hydrogen, a byproduct of the oxygen generation system, is stored or vented safely to avoid buildup.

modules.label: Command & Data Handling System
modules.explain: C&DH computers process commands, manage data, and coordinate every subsystem aboard the station.

modules.label: High Gain Antennas

fail.title: Signal to Mission Control lost
steps: Trace the high-gain antenna pointing system.

modules.explain: High gain antennas relay large amounts of data, video and voice between the ISS and mission control via relay satellites.

modules.label: Low Gain Antennas
modules.explain: Low gain antennas provide backup, lower-bandwidth communication when the high gain system is unavailable.

modules.label: Canadarm2 Robotic Arm

fail.title: Canadarm2 joint stuck mid-capture
steps: A cargo ship is waiting to be grappled.
One joint reports a torque error.
Diagnose which of the 7 joints failed.

modules.explain: Canadarm2 is a 17.6m robotic arm used to capture visiting spacecraft, move modules, and support spacewalks.

modules.label: Dextre Robotic Hand

fail.title: Dextre gripper misalignment
steps: A tool exchange fails to lock.
Camera feed shows a slight offset.

modules.explain: Dextre is a two-armed robotic 'hand' that performs delicate maintenance tasks outside without needing a spacewalk.

modules.label: External Stowage Platforms
modules.explain: External stowage platforms hold spare parts outside so astronauts don't need a spacewalk just to fetch supplies.

modules.label: Experiment Racks

fail.title: Experiment rack power interruption
steps: A running experiment loses power mid-cycle.
Check the rack's dedicated power feed.

modules.explain: Standardized racks host modular science payloads that can be swapped between Destiny, Columbus and Kibo.

modules.label: Microgravity Science Glovebox
modules.explain: The glovebox lets astronauts handle small particles, fluids or flames safely without contaminating the cabin.

modules.label: Plant Growth Chambers

fail.title: Plant growth chamber humidity spike
steps: Check humidity and LED light cycle settings.

modules.explain: Plant growth chambers test how crops grow in microgravity — vital research for future Moon and Mars food supplies.

modules.label: Crew Quarters (Sleep Pods)
modules.explain: Each astronaut has a small private sleep pod with sound insulation, ventilation and personal storage.

modules.label: Galley (Food Preparation)
modules.explain: The galley includes a food warmer and rehydration station — there's no refrigerator, so most food is dried or shelf-stable.

modules.label: Hygiene Compartment
modules.explain: Astronauts use no-rinse soap, special toilets and vacuum suction rather than showers or plumbing as on Earth.

modules.label: Exercise Treadmill (ARED)
modules.explain: Astronauts exercise about 2 hours daily using ARED and a treadmill to counteract muscle and bone loss in microgravity.

modules.label: Station Bike (CEVIS)
modules.explain: CEVIS is a stationary cycle ergometer used for cardiovascular exercise without pedals attached to the floor.

modules.label: Waste Management System

fail.title: Waste system pressure alarm
steps: Odor control filter light is on.

modules.explain: The waste management system uses airflow instead of gravity to safely handle human waste in microgravity.

modules.label: Fire Detection System

fail.title: Smoke sensor triggered
steps: An alarm sounds in the US segment.
Identify the smoke source with handheld sensors.

modules.explain: Smoke detectors and portable fire extinguishers let the crew respond within seconds, since fire behaves very differently in microgravity.

modules.label: Emergency Oxygen Supply

fail.title: Emergency oxygen mask deployment test failed
steps: A routine check shows a mask valve is stiff.
Replace or lubricate the valve mechanism.

modules.explain: Portable breathing apparatuses provide emergency oxygen during fire, depressurization or toxic atmosphere events.

modules.label: Navigation & Attitude Control

fail.title: Attitude control gyroscope drift
steps: Station orientation slowly drifts off target.
A gyroscope reports abnormal spin rate.
Diagnose which of the 4 gyroscopes is failing.

modules.explain: Gyroscopes (and thrusters as backup) keep the station correctly oriented toward the sun and Earth without using fuel.

modules.label: External Cameras & Sensors
modules.explain: External cameras help crew and ground controllers monitor docking, spacewalks, and structural health visually.

modules.label: Radiation Monitoring System

fail.title: Radiation storm warning issued
steps: A solar flare has been detected.
Guide the crew to the most shielded module.

modules.explain: During radiation storms, crew shelter in heavily shielded modules like Zvezda, since spacecraft walls alone don't block all radiation.

modules.label: Oxygen Generation System

fail.title: Oxygen generator output falling
steps: Backup oxygen candles are on standby.

modules.explain: The OGS splits water into oxygen and hydrogen via electrolysis — the hydrogen is vented or recycled, oxygen is released to the cabin.

modules.label: Water Recovery System

fail.title: Water Recovery filter clogged
steps: Check the filtration and distillation unit.

modules.explain: The WRS recycles urine, sweat and moisture from air into drinking water — recovering about 90% of water aboard.

modules.label: Carbon Dioxide Scrubbers
modules.explain: Carbon dioxide removal assemblies use absorbent beds to capture CO2 that crew members exhale, keeping air breathable.

modules.label: EVA Spacesuit Systems

fail.title: Suit cooling garment malfunction
steps: Astronaut reports overheating during a spacewalk.
Water cooling loop pressure is abnormal.

modules.explain: Spacesuits (EMUs) provide oxygen, pressure, temperature control and micrometeoroid protection during spacewalks.

modules.label: Docking Port IDA-1

fail.title: IDA-1 alignment sensor error
steps: An arriving crew capsule cannot lock in.
Sensors show a slight angle offset.
Guide the approach using camera feedback.

modules.explain: International Docking Adapters allow crew and cargo vehicles to autonomously dock or be berthed to the station.

modules.label: Docking Port IDA-2
modules.explain: A second IDA allows two crew vehicles to be docked simultaneously, increasing crew rotation flexibility.

modules.label: Docking Port IDA-3
modules.explain: IDA-3 on the Russian segment supports Soyuz and Progress vehicle dockings.
